description: Single source of truth for the Secure Image Ingestion Gate. Every ingress path (Render /api/analyze, Storage-bound client uploads, any future Edge Function image path) must defer to this file instead of maintaining its own format/size constants. This closes the size-cap drift found in Phase 1 between the style-library-images bucket (5MB) and inspiration_items.file_size_bytes (10MB DB check).
notes: This policy intentionally tightens two existing allowances found in Phase 1: (1) server.js currently allows 'image/heic' in ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES even though the client compression pipeline (services/imageUtils.js) only ever produces JPEG before upload — heic is dropped here because no repository evidence shows it is actually sent or required. (2) server.js's effective 15MB Express body cap and the 20MB app-level MAX_BASE64_BYTES check are both replaced by the tighter compressedMaxBytes values below, which are well above every observed real client output (200KB-2MB) and well below the previous ceiling.
Animated formats are disallowed for every accepted type (maxAnimationFrames=1 everywhere) because no ingress path in this repository sends or requires animated content.

Nothing here trusts filename, extension alone, Content-Type header alone, client-provided dimensions, or client-provided hashes — those are asserted server-side by the gate per docs/security/secure-image-ingestion-architecture.md.

disallowedFormats.reason: XML-based, script-execution and XXE risk; no repository evidence of use
Document format with active-content risk; no repository evidence of use
Complex/legacy container, historically high parser-vulnerability surface; no repository evidence of use
Animated by design; no repository evidence of required use
Allowed today in server.js ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES but never actually produced by the client compression pipeline (services/imageUtils.js emits JPEG only); no repository evidence it is required
Uncompressed legacy format, no repository evidence of use
zip/tar/rar/7z — not an image; disallowed unconditionally
exe/sh/bat/apk/dmg/elf/mach-o — not an image; disallowed unconditionally
mp4/mov/webm/avi — not an image; disallowed unconditionally
Any content not matching a recognized, allow-listed image signature is rejected; the gate never falls back to permissive handling for unrecognized types

requestLimits.note: This cap must be enforced while the request is still streaming in, before full in-memory buffering — see Phase 3 step 2. This closes the gap in server.js where express.json() fully buffers up to 15MB before any application-level check runs.

trustBoundaryRules: Never trust the Content-Type / declared MIME header alone — it must match the detected magic-byte signature (see extensionConsistencyRequired).
Never trust client-provided hashes — the gate computes its own SHA-256 of received bytes and of canonical output.

Never fetch or trust an image URL without server-side fetch controls (size cap, redirect limit, private-IP/SSRF denylist, content-type re-validation on the fetched bytes) — no ingress path in this repository does this today; if one is added later it must reuse this same policy file and go through the same gate, not a bespoke fetch.
